_README: THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every indexed listing field, and the evidence for every keyword in it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Keywords were being chosen in a planning document and applied to the store
by hand. Two rounds in a row shipped, or nearly shipped, words the app does not contain:
ASO_MAX_PLAN.md proposed isa, tfsa, super and asx, and all four measure ZERO in the curriculum.
A plan cannot enforce anything. This file can, because scripts/aso-keyword-truth.mjs reads it and
fails the build on an undeclared or unevidenced term.
HOW TO ADD A KEYWORD. Put it in the locale's list AND in `terms` with its evidence. There is no
way to add one without saying why it is true, which is the whole point.
VERIFY AGAINST THE STORE with `node scripts/aso-keyword-truth.mjs --live`. That fails if this file
and App Store Connect have drifted, so a hand edit in the web UI cannot silently outlive this file.
_termsNote: kind 'curriculum': the app TEACHES this. Proved by a whole-word count in src/lib/curriculum/courses/
at or above the threshold in the script. Counts below are measured, not estimated.
kind 'product': the app HAS this, but it is a feature or an audience rather than a subject, so a
curriculum count is the wrong test. Proved by a phrase in a named file that must exist.

simulator.why: The app ships a paper-trading portfolio on real market data. It is a feature, not a subject, so it measures only 18 in the corpus and must be proved against the feature instead.

teen.why: The stated audience, not a topic. AGE_FLOOR is 13 and the store description says 'for teenagers and complete beginners, aged 13 and up'.

_rejectedNote: Terms investigated and REFUSED. Recorded with the measurement that refused them so the same
argument does not have to be had twice, and so re-adding one fails loudly with the reason.
Counts are whole-word, case-insensitive, across the twelve files in src/lib/curriculum/courses/.

rejected.isa: 0 occurrences. A prefix match scores 3, and all three are the name Isaac. The UK tax wrapper is not taught anywhere in the corpus.
rejected.tfsa: 0 occurrences. The Canadian tax wrapper is not taught anywhere in the corpus.
rejected.asx: 0 occurrences. The Australian exchange is never named.
rejected.super: 28 occurrences, and every one is 'Super Bowl' or 'super-priority' in a bankruptcy lesson. Australian superannuation is not taught. A prefix match scores 217 by catching superior, supervised and superhuman, which is exactly how this nearly shipped.
rejected.roth: 708 occurrences, so it is genuinely taught, but it is a US-only term and the en-US field is already full. Available if something is dropped.
rejected.espanol: The app has no i18n: no locales key in app.json and zero getLocales calls in src/. Spanish metadata would misrepresent an English-only app under Guideline 2.3.7.
